run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:00:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing on real error signal in frontend-proxy, and the errors trace to the ad service. frontend-proxy's own ingress spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR (516.06 error vs 23,221.84 non-error ingress spans in the hour ending 10:24:04, ~2.2%; 273.33 vs 3,436.67, ~7.4%, in the 5-minute window 10:07-10:12), and its Envoy access log shows the same requests as HTTP 500 returned from upstream ("GET /api/data?... 500 - via_upstream", 21-byte body, 4-7 ms). One hop deeper, the failing operation is the ads path: frontend's GET /api/data, executing api route /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans each errored ~489 times in the window (86% error share at 10:07-10:12), while cart, checkout, product-catalog and recommendation calls from the same frontend show no error spans. The deepest observed failure is inside the ad service: its own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server spans error (473.6 vs 1,389.2 non-error over 09:00:04-10:24:04; 87% error share at 10:07-10:12, versus no ERROR series and 298.9 non-error spans at 09:45-09:50), and its container logs throw "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." (453 matching lines captured between 09:55 and 10:20), each preceded by an ad RPC line. Those failures are immediate (73% of ad error spans <=2 ms, all <=1000 ms), so this is not a timeout/latency symptom, and the ad pod is Running/ready with 0 restarts and its start time predates the alert. The exception's class/message is not in the container's stdout and change history is not integrated, so the trigger inside the ad service (most plausibly the demo fault-injection flag "adFailure", which reads "off" after the window) remains an unproven hypothesis.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own spans show the error signal behind the alert: span ingress with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR had a 1-hour increase of 516.06 at 10:24:04 against 23,221.84 non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) ingress spans in the same window (~2.2%); its client span "router frontend egress" shows 490.67 errors against 23,247.24 non-error in that window. Only STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET exist for this service.
At the height of the burst (5-minute window 10:07-10:12) frontend-proxy ingress had 273.33 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 3,436.67 non-error spans, i.e. ~7.4% of its ingress spans errored.

The frontend service has its own error spans on the ads path: "GET /api/data" STATUS_CODE_ERROR 489.15 versus UNSET 1,389.15 and client span "grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" ERROR 489.15 over 09:00:04-10:24:04; in the 5-minute window 10:07-10:12 "GET /api/data" shows 228.75 error versus 36.25 non-error spans (~86% errored).

The deepest erroring component observed is the ad service, on its own server span: service ad, span "oteldemo.AdService/GetAds", status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR 473.6 versus STATUS_CODE_UNSET 1,389.2 over 09:00:04-10:24:04; at 10:07-10:12 it is 233.75 error versus 36.25 non-error (~87% errored), while at the earlier baseline 09:45-09:50 the same query returned 298.9 non-error spans and no ERROR series.

Within the frontend the error is confined to the ads path: in the same 1-hour error query, frontend spans GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds each show ~489 errors, whereas POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations all show 0 errors.

The ad failures are immediate, not slow: of 473.6 error spans on oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, 345.6 (73%) completed in <=2 ms, 461.9 in <=400 ms and all in <=1000 ms; the matching frontend client spans put 449.5 of 489.15 errors in <=400 ms and all in <=1000 ms.

frontend-proxy's Envoy access log shows the same failures as HTTP 500 from upstream only on the ads route, e.g. "GET /api/data?contextKeys=accessories HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream with a 21-byte body and 4 ms upstream time at 10:14:54.799741Z, 10:14:56.86343Z and 10:14:58.612015Z, while /api/cart, /api/checkout, /api/products/* and /api/recommendations on the same pod returned 200 in the same seconds.

The ad service's own container logs record unhandled exceptions on ad requests: "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..." (453 matching lines captured between 09:55 and 10:20), each line preceded by an ad RPC log such as "Targeted ad request received for [binoculars]" or "Non-targeted ad request received, preparing random response.", and the exceptions are present both at 10:05:56.566Z-10:05:59.109Z and continuously in the 10:13:50-10:14:58Z sample.

The ad pod was not damaged: ad-554b849958-sk6fg is Running, all containers ready, restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-15T09:29:48Z (as are the other otel-demo pods, all started 09:29-09:31), and the ad deployment reports 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready / 1 updated; a query for Warning events in namespace otel-demo inside the authorized window returned no events (0 items processed).

The ad service is wired to the flagd feature-flag service: deployment ad runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad with env FLAGD_HOST=flagd and FLAGD_PORT=8013; deployment flagd runs ghcr.io/open-feature/flagd:v0.12.8 with command /flagd-build start --port 8013 --ofrep-port 8016 --uri file:./etc/flagd/demo.flagd.json, mounts ConfigMap flagd-config, and also runs a flagd-ui container.

The flagd config served through ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json, read at 10:25) contains a fault-injection flag "adFailure" described as "Fail ad service" with variants off/on; at read time its defaultVariant is "off", as are adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure and the other fault flags.

The ad service's GetAds handler threw an unhandled exception for most calls during the burst (~87% of ad GetAds spans errored at 10:07-10:12, each failure <=1 s, 73% <=2 ms), which is the signature of the otel-demo fault-injection flag "adFailure" ("Fail ad service") being switched on through flagd/flagd-ui and later off: the ConfigMap read after the window shows defaultVariant "off", but there is no change history to prove it was "on" during the burst, so this remains unconfirmed.

The flagd dependency itself shows no failure burst: the flagd pod is Running with both containers ready, restartCount 0 and startTime 09:31:42Z, and the ad service's own flagd client span "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (a client span of service ad) rose only from ~1.02 to ~2.03 errors per 1-hour window across 10:00-10:24; fraud-detection and recommendation flagd EventStream error series were 3.05 and 3.05 over the whole 84-minute window, i.e. chronic single-digit-per-hour noise rather than an outage.

Rejected: the ad service was crashed, OOM-killed, evicted or rolled out during the window. Pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg has restartCount 0 and startTime 09:29:48Z (before the alert), the ad deployment shows 1/1 available and ready, and the Warning-event query for namespace otel-demo in the authorized window returned no events (no OOMKilling/Evicted/FailedScheduling observed).

Rejected: the errors are client deadlines or cancellations caused by the ad service becoming slow (e.g. adHighCpu or adManualGc). The ad server spans that errored were short - 73% <=2 ms, all <=1000 ms - and the frontend's client error spans were also short (449.5 of 489.15 <=400 ms), while ad GetAds already ran at similar fast latencies at the 09:45-09:50 baseline, so spans failed instead of timing out.

Other backends show no error signal of their own in this window: accounting 'orders receive', payment GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect and fraud-detection ResolveInt ERROR series all read 0 over 09:00:04-10:24:04 (the only non-zero entries in that query are the chronic flagd EventStream series). No STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were returned at all for cart, checkout, currency, email, product-catalog, quote or shipping, which is unknown rather than proven zero.

gaps: Change history is not integrated in this Run, so it cannot be verified whether (or exactly when) the flagd flag "adFailure" or the flagd-config ConfigMap changed around 10:00-10:06Z; the fault-injection hypothesis therefore stays unproven.

The ad container's stdout contains only the line "Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@..."; no throwable class, message or stack trace and no flagd-related line was found, so the internal reason for the exception inside the ad service is unknown.

When the exception burst began is not established: the ad pod log queries for 09:35:00-10:00:00 and 10:03:00-10:05:00 returned no_data (not zero matches), and greps for stack-trace/keyword text in the ad logs likewise returned no_data; only the presence of exceptions at 10:05:56-10:05:59 and 10:13:50-10:14:58 is observed.

No alerting rule named RequestErrorRate was returned by the Prometheus rules API (empty/no_data), so the alert expression is unknown and the reported value 2.111 could not be reproduced from span metrics (1-hour ingress error share ~2.2%, 5-minute share at 10:12 ~7.4%).

Jaeger only held traces up to about 09:44:10 (the returned frontend and frontend-proxy traces are from 09:44:08-09:44:10) and a traces_search_by_tags error=true query for 09:55-10:20 returned no_data, so the failing trace graph during the error window is unknown.
The frontend container produced no readable log lines in 09:58-10:10 (a no_data query), so the frontend-side error text behind the HTTP 500 on /api/data is unknown.
Container and node resource metrics (CPU, memory, GC) were not part of the metric set explored, so adHighCpu / adManualGc style resource pressure on the ad service could not be evaluated directly.
The flagd pod's own container logs returned no_data, so flagd-side evidence about serving flag updates during the window is unavailable.

Whether the ad failures continued after the captured data ends is unknown: the ad and frontend-proxy pod logs stop at 10:14:58 and the frontend-proxy span-metric series are flat from ~10:17:04 to the last sample at 10:24:04.
next_steps: Correlate the 10:00-10:10Z window with the flagd/flagd-ui audit log, GitOps commit history or operator actions on the otel-demo 'adFailure' flag to confirm or drop the fault-injection hypothesis.
Inspect the ad service's stderr/exception handler output (or enable stack-trace logging) to capture the throwable class and message behind the 'Exception while executing runnable ...' lines.
Look up the RequestErrorRate alerting rule in its rule file/repository to learn the exact expression behind the reported 2.111 value.

Restore frontend and flagd container log collection so the frontend's 500 error text and flagd's flag-evaluation activity can be read, and re-check a longer metric window to verify whether the errors stopped after 10:15Z.
